title: Checkout Phase 1: server-verified step gating + PaymentSection readiness guard
description: Phase 1 of the front_store-9ze fix. Diagnostic showed customers can reach Payment (and be charged) while Saleor lacks email/shipping address/emirate/billing/delivery method, then checkoutComplete rejects: money taken, no order. Gate goNext() on a network-only checkout fetch with per-field bilingual messages, and guard PaymentSection so no gateway mounts on a non-ready checkout (bypass for processingPayment redirect-return). Does NOT fix the emirate label, debounce, or form saves (Phase 2).
notes: Committed locally efdff70 + c025924, NOT pushed/deployed. Live tests vs production API: T1 normal Stripe flow completed -> Order #40 (test mode), both gates passed first fetch; T2 rushed shipping blocked with emirate message; T3 payment guard blocked COD+Stripe with zero payment mutations; T4 redirect-return on open checkout not blocked (reconciliation ran); T4 on completed checkout -> stuck overlay, pre-existing (reproduced on live site), filed separately. Close after deploy + production smoke check.
close_reason: Deployed via PR #38 and verified live on tawasiplus.com (visible pane): Contact->Shipping advances in ~2s, rushed Shipping with default emirate is blocked with the emirate message. The earlier reported hang was a false alarm (hidden Browser pane froze requestAnimationFrame).

title: [bug] /login and /register 500 — Server Component passes function prop to Client Component
description: Both (main)/login/page.tsx and (main)/register/page.tsx are async Server Components (call cookies()/redirect()/getTranslations) that render <AuthFormWrapper mode="login" onModeChange={() => undefined} />. AuthFormWrapper.tsx is a Client Component ("use client"). Passing an inline arrow function as a prop from a Server Component to a Client Component is invalid under Next.js 15's RSC model and throws server-side on every request: 'Error: Event handlers cannot be passed to Client Component props ... digest: 3534376298'. Confirmed live in session 34 (account-deletion work) via a fresh next dev run with .next cache fully cleared, so this is not stale-build noise -- it reproduces from a clean build. Net effect: every visit to /login or /register currently 500s for any visitor, on both locales. This directly matches unverified checklist item 9 in front_store-u40 (Verify auth flow end-to-end), which has been open and unclaimed since session 8 -- this bug likely existed undetected the whole time. Fix: make AuthFormWrapper's onModeChange prop optional with an internal no-op default, and drop the onModeChange={() => undefined} passed from both standalone pages (AuthModal.tsx's own usage, which passes setAuthModalMode client-to-client, is fine and must not be touched).
acceptance_criteria: Fresh next dev + cleared .next: /en/uae-channel/login and /en/uae-channel/register both render the form with zero console/server errors, in both en and ar. pnpm tsc --noEmit clean, pnpm lint at baseline (<=7 warnings, all pre-existing in src/checkout/ + Logo.tsx).
close_reason: Fixed on hotfix/login-register-rsc-crash: AuthFormWrapper's onModeChange made optional with a no-op default; both standalone pages' inline onModeChange={() => undefined} removed. Verified live: /en+/ar /login and /register both render with zero console/server errors on a fresh next dev + cleared .next. tsc clean, lint at baseline.

title: Readiness check fail-open broken for network/HTTP/GraphQL errors: failed urql re-read replaces checkout view with not-found
description: Found while verifying the fail-open observability record (Phase 2 pre-push verification). useCheckoutReadiness re-reads the checkout with client.query(CheckoutDocument, same variables, network-only), which shares its urql operation key with every mounted useCheckout(). When that request fails with a network error (reproduced by rejecting the readiness fetch in a production build against the production API), urql publishes the error result under the shared key: useCheckout()'s data becomes undefined, so views/Checkout/Checkout.tsx renders PageNotFound ('We couldn't fetch information about your checkout') instead of the wizard advancing. goNext did fail open and logged [checkout-readiness:fail-open] {reason: network, attempts: 1, elapsedMs: 1, source: step-advance}, but the page is gone; a reload recovers (checkout intact). Expected to apply equally to HTTP and GraphQL errors (error result without data); timeouts DO fail open correctly (verified: step-advance record at 8.0s, advance at 8.4s; payment-guard record, gateways at 17.1s; a hung request also dedupes both checks onto one in-flight key). Behaviour dates from Phase 1 (live via PR #38), not introduced by Phase 2. Direction (unverified): read through a request that does not share the useCheckout operation key (e.g. a distinct document/variables or a plain fetch with deduplicated fragments - see the discarded hotfix: raw print of CheckoutDocument duplicates the Money fragment and Saleor returns 400), so a failed check cannot overwrite the page's checkout data.

title: Checkout Phase 2: commit-on-advance + emirate root cause + form-save bugs
description: Phase 2 of front_store-9ze (Phase 1 gating front_store-0ev is live and verified). Fix the causes so customers stop hitting the Phase 1 block: (1) emirate select - countryAreaType 'emirate' unmapped -> no label/placeholder -> browser shows 'Abu Dhabi' while value is ''; audit other unmapped types; (2) stale-closure validation in useAutoSaveAddressForm.partialSubmit, Select overriding passed onBlur, inverted email check in useGuestUserForm, stuck 'loading' scopes after canceled debounced writes, duplicate EN/AR emirate options; (3) commit-on-advance: each step form hook exposes commit() that cancels the debounce and saves current values immediately; goNext awaits commits then runs the Phase 1 assertion; fix useDebouncedSubmit newer-instance cancel bug; (4) fold in readiness hardening: bounded verify + fail-open on verification errors. Out of scope: redundant refetch (needs Graphcache), UI/visual changes.
notes: Committed locally 9f68ca6 (Phase 2) + 5c74ba0 (COD reminder marker fix) + bfdd9b2 (docs) + pre-push verification docs; NOT pushed. Pre-push verification (visible pane, production build vs production API): billing in-flight guard - 6 runs (3 logged-in, 3 guest; second change at refetch +0/+300/+1000ms) all left Saleor billing == final shipping before and after advancing; true-guest Stripe Order #45 completed (AED 19.99, billing==shipping, no COD reminder). Orders created: #40 #42 #43 #44 #45 (recorded in CLAUDE.md). Found: front_store-auc (fail-open broken for network errors, pre-existing from Phase 1); front_store-057 re-verified real. Fail-open observability record (item 3) implemented but left UNCOMMITTED pending user diff review. Close after deploy + live smoke.

title: Stripe redirect return on an already-completed checkout: 'Almost done...' overlay stuck forever
description: Found while live-testing Phase 1 (front_store-0ev) test 4. When the page loads with processingPayment=true (Stripe return_url) but the checkout has already been converted into an order (e.g. Stripe's webhook safety net completed it first, or the customer reloads the return URL after completion), checkout(id:) returns null, so views/Checkout/Checkout.tsx renders PageNotFound ('We couldn't fetch information about your checkout') - but PaymentProcessingScreen (RootViews.tsx) wraps it and its fixed full-screen 'Almost done...' overlay stays up forever, hiding even the 'Go back to store' button. The order exists and payment succeeded, yet the customer sees an endless spinner with no way to their confirmation. Reproduced on BOTH the local Phase 1 build and the live tawasiplus.com (pre-Phase-1 code), using checkout Q2hlY2tvdXQ6Zjg2NDZmY2YtYjY3Ny00YmM5LWIzNzMtZDgwZGQxZmY2ZDdh (Order #40, a Stripe test-mode order) - so pre-existing, not caused by Phase 1. Likely fix direction (unverified): when processingPayment is set and checkout(id:) is null, look up the order by checkout token / redirect to OrderConfirmation instead of PageNotFound, and never leave the overlay up over PageNotFound.
notes: RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-14 WITH PANE VISIBLE (production build vs production API, localhost copy): REAL, not a hidden-pane artifact. Return-from-Stripe URL (processingPayment=true, payment_intent, transaction) for already-completed checkout Q2hlY2tvdXQ6Zjg2NDZmY2YtYjY3Ny00YmM5LWIzNzMtZDgwZGQxZmY2ZDdh (Order #40): document visible, rAF at ~60fps (max frame gap 19ms) for 30s, 'Almost done...' overlay visible the whole time over Checkout.tsx's PageNotFound text; elementFromPoint at the 'Go back to store' button hits the overlay (button unreachable). Not fixed (verification-only session).

title: Debounced checkout field updates (delivery method, email, address) can be silently lost if customer advances quickly
description:
Discovered during Session 49's checkoutComplete retry-loop investigation (front_store, see CLAUDE.md Known Issues + Checkout Sub-App section).

useDebouncedSubmit (src/checkout/hooks/useDebouncedSubmit.ts) debounces field-update mutations by 2 seconds. The Shipping/Contact step's component tree fully unmounts the moment the wizard advances (AnimatePresence + key={currentStep} in CheckoutForm.tsx), which triggers useDebouncedSubmit's cleanup effect and CANCELS any still-pending debounced call outright -- not defers it, cancels it.

This means a customer who moves through Contact or Shipping faster than ~2 seconds (very achievable -- Aramex is pre-selected by default, so a fast customer might just click through without any pause) can reach Payment with that field NEVER PERSISTED server-side, even though the UI showed it as filled/selected the whole time. Confirmed live in production via a genuine UI walkthrough (no GraphQL shortcuts): reached a real checkout with chargeStatus:FULL (COD's transactionInitialize succeeds unconditionally, doesn't check this) and email:null.

This affects at least three forms sharing the same useDebouncedSubmit pattern:
- useDeliveryMethodsForm.ts (delivery method)
- useCheckoutEmailUpdate.ts (email)
- useAddressListForm.ts (address)

Session 49 fixed the SYMPTOM (usePayments.ts's infinite checkoutComplete retry loop that resulted from this), but deliberately did not fix this underlying race -- out of that fix's scope. Fields can still silently fail to persist; they just no longer cause a runaway retry loop when checkoutComplete then rejects the (now correctly failing, gracefully surfaced) completion attempt.

Possible directions for a future fix (not decided, needs its own investigation): flush the debounced submit on unmount instead of canceling it (debounce.flush() before cancel in the cleanup effect), or block wizard advancement until the pending mutation resolves, or increase the debounce window's safety margin. Needs its own root-cause session -- do not assume any of these is correct without verifying.
close_reason: Root cause: the emirate select. Saleor's AE countryAreaType 'emirate' had no label mapping in useAddressFormUtils, so the field had no label/placeholder, Select rendered no empty option, and the browser displayed 'Abu Dhabi' while formik's countryArea stayed ''. Required validation then failed and useAutoSaveAddressForm never saved the guest shipping address at all (no shipping methods, billing or delivery method followed). Compounded by stale-closure validation in partialSubmit, Select dropping the passed onBlur, and 2s debounced saves cancelled on step unmount. Fixed in two phases: Phase 1 server-verified gating (front_store-0ev, live via PR #38) and Phase 2 commit-on-advance + emirate/form fixes (front_store-bwh, commit 9f68ca6, verified against production API). Remaining deploy tracked on front_store-bwh.

title: Stripe checkout: transactionProcess never fires, null.id TypeError in stripeElementsForm.tsx
description:
During the Session 47 'Final Combined Fix' test loop (redirect-aware gateway selection + safety-net token), discovered that the primary Stripe reconciliation path never actually works: transactionProcess is never called successfully client-side.

Reproduced across 3 separate real test orders (#28 non-redirect, #29 forced 3DS redirect via test card 4000002500003155, #30 non-redirect clean-signal test) on production (tawasiplus.com) after both this session's fixes were deployed:
- Saleor's own webhook-dispatch debug log shows ZERO 'Sending payload...for event transaction_process_session' lines, despite the app's Webhook row (id 106, com.tawasiplus.stripe_payment) being correctly subscribed to that event (confirmed via Django shell).
- proton-payments' own request log likewise shows zero transaction_process_session hits.
- Browser console (read_console_messages, captured right after clicking Pay on order #30) showed a repeated client-side error immediately after payment submission: 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading id)', originating from the Stripe checkout bundle chunks (4718-f447e6003ff46ae7.js and 7cf2dd7c-2503145de182659a.js).

Root cause hypothesis (not yet fixed, not yet fully isolated): something in stripeElementsForm.tsx's post-confirmPayment flow reads .id off a value that's null (likely the transaction id sourced from getUrlForTransactionInitialize() or the URL's transaction param) before calling transactionProcess({id: transactionId}) — throwing before the GraphQL request is ever sent, which is consistent with Saleor never seeing an incoming mutation at all.

Impact: every Stripe order on production is currently being completed ONLY via the async Stripe-webhook safety net (reportTransactionEvent, Session 47's Fix 2), not via the synchronous transactionProcess path the code is designed around. This works today because Stripe's own webhook is reliable, but it means there is no redundancy left \u2014 if Stripe's webhook were ever delayed or failed, a customer would be stuck on the 'Almost done...' overlay indefinitely despite Fix 1 (redirect-aware gateway selection) correctly getting them back to the Payment step.

This file (src/checkout/sections/PaymentSection/StripeElements/stripeElementsForm.tsx) is on this project's do-not-touch-without-explicit-approval list, so it was left unmodified. User explicitly chose to file this rather than fix it in Session 47.

All 3 real Stripe test PaymentIntents from this diagnosis were refunded and all 4 test orders (#28-#31) canceled during Session 47's cleanup.
notes:
RESOLVED (Session 48). Root cause precisely identified: src/checkout/hooks/useCheckoutComplete.ts line 9 destructured checkout.id from useCheckout() with no null guard. useCheckout() legitimately returns checkout:null once a checkout has been converted into an Order (a real state, not hypothetical) -- Stripe's async webhook safety net (Session 47 Fix 2) can finish that conversion before the browser's own confirmPayment()->transactionProcess->onCheckoutComplete() chain gets back around to a render. useCheckoutComplete is called unconditionally by every payment method (Stripe, Adyen, COD, DummyDropIn), so the crash was reachable from all of them, though only Stripe's async-safety-net race made it likely in practice.

Fix: guarded the destructure (checkout?.id), and added an explicit guard in the returned onCheckoutComplete callback that short-circuits with a graceful payment.unexpectedError toast instead of ever calling submit() when checkoutId is absent -- necessary because useSubmit()'s own internal handleSubmit ALSO reads checkout.id/checkout.channel.slug unconditionally (same latent bug, one level down, in a hook outside this session's approval scope) and would have thrown the identical crash if reached with a null checkout.

Item 4 (red 'duplicate/failed' banner on OrderConfirmation): searched the entire codebase, found no UI string matching that description. Believe it is the user's description of the existing payment.unexpectedError toast (confirmed real, and displayed by the exact code path this fix now guards) rather than a second, separate bug -- could not confirm with certainty against the actual customer-facing screen.

Verified live (local dev pointed at production Saleor/proton-payments, since this session's instructions were commit-only-do-not-push): order #34 -- checkout genuinely transitioned to null mid-flow (confirmed via checkout(id) query returning null immediately after), onCheckoutComplete completed cleanly with zero errors, chargeStatus FULL, no crash. This is the exact race the bug depended on, occurring naturally without needing a forced redirect delay.

transaction_process_session webhook still does not appear in proton-payments' logs even post-fix -- re-analyzed and this is now understood to be EXPECTED Saleor behavor (the resolver skips re-invoking the app webhook when the transaction is already resolved via the async safety net), not a bug. The client's own transactionProcess mutation call does succeed and drives checkoutComplete correctly, evidenced by order 34 completing via the primary path with no crash.

tsc clean, lint clean (6 pre-existing warnings, none new). Only src/checkout/hooks/useCheckoutComplete.ts changed (git diff --name-only confirmed). Committed locally, not pushed per explicit instruction (payment-critical, awaiting review).
close_reason: Fixed in Session 48: guarded checkout.id destructure in useCheckoutComplete.ts + onCheckoutComplete guard. See issue notes for full root cause and verification.

title: Phone OTP login option on LoginForm (email/phone tabs)
description: Added a second login path alongside email/password: LoginForm.tsx gained an Email/Phone tab; phone mode is send-code -> verify-code via proton_identity's OTP endpoints and Saleor's externalObtainAccessTokens (com.tawasiplus.phone-auth plugin). New routes: POST /api/otp/send (proxies proton_identity, reuses identity.ts's callIdentityService) and POST /api/auth/phone-login (calls the Saleor mutation directly, public/no SERVICE_TOKEN, reuses the existing setAuthCookies helper).
design: Deliberately uniform INVALID_OR_EXPIRED_CODE for every phone-login failure (wrong/expired/already-consumed code, or a verified-but-unregistered phone) — preserves the anti-enumeration ambiguity proton_auth_plugin's plugin already builds in; the route and the UI must not be more specific than the plugin itself is. Resend cooldown UI (60s) mirrors proton_identity's real server-side window but the server remains authoritative. proton_identity outage on /otp/send degrades gracefully with a 'switch to email' escape hatch; the email/password tab is completely unaffected by a proton_identity outage.
acceptance_criteria: Verified live: full real send->verify->login round trip against a registered phone issues a real session; loaded the checkout sub-app with that session afterward and confirmed Session 38's cookie-bridge customer-recognition (Contact step shows the signed-in account) works identically to a password-issued token. Wrong code, DB-forced expired code, and a correctly-verified-but-unregistered phone all produce the byte-identical error, confirmed both at the API and in the rendered UI. Stopped proton_identity and confirmed /api/otp/send fails gracefully (clear message + switch-to-email link, no crash) while email/password login keeps working unaffected. pnpm tsc --noEmit and pnpm lint both clean (baseline 7 warnings unchanged, all pre-existing in src/checkout/), src/checkout/ untouched.
close_reason: Implemented and verified live this session — see design/acceptance notes.

title: Wire PHONE_IDENTITY_SERVICE_URL/TOKEN + proton_identity into production before launch
description: This session (front_store-98v) wired the storefront to proton_identity locally only. Before production launch: (1) confirm production PHONE_IDENTITY_SERVICE_URL/PHONE_IDENTITY_SERVICE_TOKEN env vars match the real value set on proton_identity's production deployment (mirrors the WEBHOOK_SECRET replication discipline documented for proton-payments), (2) confirm proton_identity is actually deployed/reachable in production the way saleor_platform/README.md's proton_identity section describes for local Docker, (3) decide whether email confirmation stays enabled in production (this session found it enabled locally, which is the harder/more-tested code path since the phone write can't happen atomically at registration in that case — but production's actual site setting should be confirmed, not assumed).
acceptance_criteria: Production env vars set and confirmed matching; proton_identity confirmed reachable from the production storefront's server-side routes; a real registration + login-gate flow smoke-tested against production.

title: Mandatory phone number: registration + login-gate (proton_identity)
description: Phone is now required at registration and enforced via a login-gate (PhoneGate.tsx), backed by the proton_identity service. accountRegister has no phone field, so the write is always post-login: RegisterForm fires it immediately after auto-login (confirmation-disabled path), or best-effort carries it via localStorage (pendingPhone.ts) for LoginForm to flush after email confirmation. PhoneGate is the guaranteed fallback for any user who reaches login without a phone on file (new account, cross-device confirmation, or a failed carry-forward), and is fail-open on proton_identity outages (GET /api/identity/phone-status returns hasPhone:true on any error — never lock a user out over an infra outage).
design: New routes: POST /api/identity/set-phone, GET /api/identity/phone-status (both server-side proxies to proton_identity via src/lib/identity.ts, 3s timeout). New shared component PhoneField.tsx (RegisterForm + PhoneGate). PhoneSaveNoticeBanner.tsx uses a window event (phoneSaveNotice.ts), not AuthContext state — router.refresh() remounts AuthProvider and silently drops context-based fire-and-forget callbacks, confirmed live during testing. Full design rationale in CLAUDE.md under 'Mandatory Phone Number — Registration + Login-Gate'.
acceptance_criteria: All mandatory test paths verified live: valid-phone registration (confirmation-required path, verified via direct proton_identity GET /phones/status), invalid-phone registration still succeeds, existing phoneless user gets gated then unblocks without reload and doesn't re-trigger, 409 conflict shows distinct message, proton_identity outage fails open on both read and write paths with a non-blocking banner, and a caught user gets resolved (silently same-device, or via the gate cross-device) once the service recovers. pnpm tsc --noEmit and pnpm lint both clean (0 new warnings, baseline 7 unchanged), src/checkout/ untouched.
notes: Confirmation-disabled auto-login path was verified by temporarily toggling Saleor's enable_account_confirmation_by_email site setting via Django shell (reverted after) — this environment defaults to confirmation-required.
close_reason: Implemented and verified live this session — see design/acceptance notes.

title: [bug] SALEOR_APP_TOKEN in .env no longer authenticates - every [channel] page 500s locally
description: generateStaticParams in src/app/[locale]/[channel]/layout.tsx calls ChannelsList with SALEOR_APP_TOKEN. Saleor now returns PermissionDenied (AUTHENTICATED_APP/AUTHENTICATED_STAFF_USER required), executeGraphQL throws, and EVERY page under [channel] returns 500 in local dev. Discovered in session 44; unrelated to that session's code. Temporary workaround while testing was to comment the var out so generateStaticParams falls back to default-channel, but that in turn breaks 'next build' on /ar/default-channel/account (a cookies-using route). Fix: regenerate an app token in the Saleor Dashboard and update .env. Verify with: curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/graphql/ -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' -d '{"query":"{ channels { slug } }"}'
close_reason: Disproven by a follow-up audit (2026-09-04/05): the token is valid and authenticates fine (200, returns default-channel/uae-channel). The 500s were caused by a local networking fault, not authorization — VS Code's auto port-forward on 127.0.0.1:8000 black-holes requests, competing with Docker's 0.0.0.0 listener and wslrelay's [::1] listener on the same port; whichever localhost resolves to determines success/failure. The app token also already holds 10 permissions including MANAGE_CHANNELS, contradicting this issue's premise that it's scoped narrowly. Real fix: stop VS Code's auto-forward on port 8000 (or pin to a stable address), not regenerating the token.

title: Checkout customer recognition — logged-in users treated as guests
description: Logged-in customers (valid saleor_token cookie) were treated as guests at /checkout — shown the register/login prompt, saved addresses never offered. Root cause: the checkout sub-app (src/checkout/) authenticates through an isolated @saleor/auth-sdk client (mounted in src/app/[locale]/checkout/layout.tsx), completely separate from the main app's custom saleor_token/saleor_refresh_token auth system. The checkout's customer-recognition logic (useUser, useCustomerAttach, UserShippingAddressSection) was already fully built and correct — it was inert only because the SDK's client never received a valid access token.
design: Fix implemented entirely in src/middleware.ts (no src/checkout/ files touched). @saleor/auth-sdk's SaleorAuthClient.fetchWithAuth has a built-in one-shot bridge: it reads a plain, non-httpOnly cookie literally named 'token' via document.cookie on first use, adopts it as the access token, then deletes the cookie itself. Middleware now sets this 'token' cookie (non-httpOnly, sameSite lax, maxAge 60s) whenever the request path is /checkout (locale-prefixed) AND a valid saleor_token is present — using the freshly-refreshed token if the existing silent-refresh logic just ran. Guests and every other route are unaffected; the cookie is never set when saleor_token is absent.
acceptance_criteria: Verified live: logged-in customer reaching /checkout sees the signedInUser Contact step (not guest prompt); checkoutCustomerAttach mutation fires with zero errors and attaches the real user; UserShippingAddressSection renders the customer's saved address as a selectable option; guest checkout unaffected when logged out; the bridge 'token' cookie is confirmed absent on every non-checkout page (homepage, PDP, cart, products) both logged in and out. pnpm tsc --noEmit: 0 errors. pnpm lint: 6 warnings (baseline, all pre-existing in src/checkout/). git diff confirms zero files under src/checkout/ touched.
close_reason: Fixed via middleware-only bridge cookie; verified live end-to-end (session 38)

title: Add real GA4 measurement ID before launch

title: [bug] Account confirmation + password reset email links land on homepage instead of the intended page
description: Diagnostic session confirmed: RegisterForm.tsx and ForgotPasswordForm.tsx both built redirectUrl as ${origin}/reset-password, omitting the required /{locale}/{channel} path segments. next-intl + the App Router then misrouted the link (the bare path was interpreted as locale+channel, matching the homepage route instead of reset-password/confirm-account). Additionally, no account-confirmation page or confirmAccount mutation call existed anywhere in the app at all — confirmation emails had nowhere valid to land regardless of the redirectUrl bug.
close_reason: Fixed. redirectUrl construction in RegisterForm.tsx/ForgotPasswordForm.tsx now includes /{locale}/{channel} via useLocale()+useParams(). Added the missing account-confirmation flow: confirmAccount mutation (introspected from schema, not assumed), src/graphql/mutations/AccountConfirm.graphql + codegen, src/app/api/auth/confirm-account/route.ts, src/app/[locale]/[channel]/(main)/confirm-account/page.tsx + ConfirmAccountClient.tsx, confirmAccount i18n namespace (en+ar). Verified live end-to-end: both forms' captured fetch payloads now carry correctly-scoped redirectUrl, and /confirm-account renders pending/success/error states correctly in both en and ar (RTL). tsc: 0 errors. lint: 6 warnings (under the 7 baseline).

title: [bug] .env SMTP config points to live production Zoho mailbox, not local Mailpit
description: front_store/.env has a comment above the SMTP_* vars saying 'dev: Mailpit on localhost:1025', but the actual configured values are SMTP_HOST=smtp.zoho.com, SMTP_USER=info@tawasiplus.com, SMTP_PASS=<real password> -- real production credentials for the live info@tawasiplus.com mailbox, not Mailpit. Discovered while live-testing the new /api/account-deletion-feedback route (Session 34 revision): a test request from a throwaway diag-*@example.com account actually delivered to the real inbox instead of showing up in Mailpit (checked, confirmed absent). /api/contact shares this exact transporter config/pattern, so it is equally affected -- any local dev testing of the contact form has been sending real emails to production the whole time, not just this new route. Risk: (1) real inbox gets test/junk emails during dev work, (2) no way to verify email flows locally without live delivery, (3) production SMTP password sits in a local .env file that may be less tightly controlled than deployment secrets. Fix: point .env's SMTP_HOST/PORT at localhost:1025 (Mailpit, already running in the local Saleor docker stack) for local dev, and move the real Zoho credentials to server-only env (already presumably configured correctly in production deployment -- verify separately). Do not touch server/production env as part of this fix.
acceptance_criteria: Local .env SMTP_HOST points at Mailpit (localhost:1025) or another local catcher. A test email sent via /api/contact or /api/account-deletion-feedback while running locally shows up in Mailpit (http://localhost:8025) and does NOT appear in the real info@tawasiplus.com inbox. Production/server env verified separately to still have the real Zoho credentials (this fix must not accidentally break live email sending).

title: Verify auth flow end-to-end (Session 8 smoke test)

value: Claude Browser pane gotcha: when the in-app Browser pane is HIDDEN, document.visibilityState is 'hidden' and requestAnimationFrame never fires (timers and fetch still run). The checkout wizard's framer-motion AnimatePresence mode='wait' step transition then never finishes, so the UI freezes on the previous step's last frame (e.g. a stuck 'Checking your details...' button) and looks exactly like a hang. This caused a false production-outage alarm and an unnecessary rollback/hotfix during Phase 1 (front_store-0ev). Before trusting any UI timing/hang observation, assert document.visibilityState==='visible' and that a requestAnimationFrame callback fires (take a screenshot to make the pane render).
